artifacts.summary: Restored Gate 8 as a usable binary signal: sealed test-gate-lock.sh's teardown-case ordering (assert process death via kill -0 rather than inferring it), reconciled two stale known-failures.txt rows (one kept-and-updated for a newly-discovered, now-fixed coverage gap), ran the full unscoped battery twice with zero NEW failures, and redeployed twice to RESULT=landed_verify_clean.

completion_data.completion_summary: Made test-gate-lock.sh's aggregate-only flake unreproducible (6/6 clean reproduction attempts) and hardened its teardown-case ordering anyway; reconciled known-failures.txt (removed one stale row, updated-then-removed another after fixing its real underlying gap in suite-classification.data); verified two full, unscoped run-all.sh --fail-on-new runs report zero NEW failures and verify-deploy.sh passes in full with deploy-headless.sh reaching RESULT=landed_verify_clean.

memory_candidates.content: Before trusting a research report's 'fails only when run concurrently with its file-scope siblings' framing for a shell-suite flake, check run-all.sh's own LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES scheduling: a suite in that list runs fully serially before the parallel pool starts and can NEVER overlap with sibling suites within one run-all.sh invocation, regardless of --only selection. If the suite is already load-sensitive, the real trigger for an 'aggregate-only' failure must be external ambient host load at measurement time (e.g. other concurrent /orchestrate dispatches), not intra-run sibling contention -- re-attempting reproduction under today's load, and reasoning about the actual scheduling code, is cheaper than assuming the report's framing is still accurate.

A suite whose own lint/check resolves its subject via a 'deploy-tree-first' pattern (common_test_resolve_subject) will NOT reflect a source-store-only fix until the next redeploy propagates it to .claude/. Before removing a known-failures.txt row on the strength of such a fix, either redeploy first and re-verify standalone, or explicitly keep the row (with an updated, accurate reason) until the redeploy has actually landed -- removing it prematurely makes a still-genuinely-red suite silently NEW/undeclared.
